name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent on *all* PRs—open and merged—for two weeks. It catches edge cases missed by humans and automated checks, improving review consistency. The trade-off is temporary noise in PR comments, but the data quality gain outweighs it.

name: Gauge
text: PR-Agent on *all* PRs risks normalizing noise—reviewers will ignore *all* comments, including real issues, once the false-positive flood starts. Shadow mode trains reviewers to filter noise *now*; rolling it out site-wide without proving it catches *meaningful* misses first is gambling with review quality. Settle it: run PR-Agent on *only* the 20% most error-prone PRs by historical data for two weeks, measure the signal-to-noise ratio, then decide.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *only* PRs from new contributors for two weeks to measure its real impact on review quality without risking noise overload. If it catches meaningful misses there, expand to all PRs—cheaper than a full rollout, faster than waiting for merged PRs to accumulate.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *only* new-contributor PRs for two weeks. This tests its real impact without flooding reviewers with noise. If it catches meaningful misses, we expand to all PRs—cheaper and faster than waiting for merged PRs to pile up. The trade-off is delayed full coverage, but the risk of normalizing noise is too high to gamble on a full rollout now.
